title: Cohorted Entropy‑Guided Exposure Controller for Safe Model Rollouts
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Build an A/B experiment controller that combines canary rollouts, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback using adaptive exposure driven by per-cohort output entropy and quality signals. The controller should enable per-tenant caps and staged exposure with Bayesian sequential stats checks and safety gates.
background: Current rollouts rely on static traffic splits and offline analyses. That leads to slower detection of regressions and coarse exposure controls for multi-tenant customers. We need a unified experiment controller that: 1) increments exposure automatically when quality and safety signals are stable, 2) routes shadow traffic for offline scoring, 3) supports per-cohort and per-tenant policies, and 4) auto-rolls back when degradation is detected.
proposal: Implement a "dual-path" experiment runner: live A/B path for real requests and a shadow path for mirrored traffic to gather offline signals. Use entropy (token-level and sequence-level) and signal aggregators (latency, top-k divergence, prompt-specific metrics) to compute a continuous risk score. Exposure increases follow a PID-like controller with a conservative growth rate and caps. Statistical checks use Bayesian sequential testing (posterior probability that new model is worse by delta > threshold) and a real-time early-stop that triggers rollback or freeze.
rollout_strategy:
- Start with 0% exposure in a shadow-only preview for 24-48 hours.
- Promote to a tiny canary (0.1–0.5%) for targeted cohorts.
- Apply cohort-aware ramp: cohorts with historically stable metrics get faster ramps.
- Use entropy-based gating: if sequence entropy increases > X sigma vs baseline, pause ramp.
- Allow manual override and enforced recovery window before next attempt.
statistical_checks:
- Primary test: Bayesian superiority test on a composite quality score (Q) with prior calibrated from historical stable releases.
- Secondary tests: latency distribution shift (KS test), hallucination proxy (semantic similarity drop), and safety token hits.
- Sequential stopping: compute posterior every N requests; if P(model_worse_by_delta)>0.95 -> auto-rollback.
- Minimum sample per cohort: 1k completed requests or configurable.
exposure_control_config:
- default_ramp: [0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10]
- max_per_tenant: configurable (default 0.2)
- entropy_thresholds: sequence_delta_sigma=3
- ramp_backoff: exponential with base 0.5
- cooldown_window: 2 hours after a pause or rollback
metrics_and_alerts:
- Dashboard panels: exposure %, per-cohort Q score, entropy delta, latency p99, safety token rate.
- Alert policies:
  * P(Q_degradation>delta)>0.90 for 30m -> P1 page
  * Latency p99 increase > 2x baseline -> P2
  * Safety token rate > 0.1% -> P0 immediate halt
- Audit logs for every exposure change with actor (auto/manual) and linked evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- UI: experiment creation flow supporting shadow-only preview, cohort selection, and per-tenant caps.
- Backend: controller service that can adjust exposure in real time and emit decision events to audit log.
- Statistical engine returns posterior updates at 1s granularity for 50k req/min workloads (approx). 
- Auto-rollback triggers verified in canary playbook with simulated regression dataset.
- End-to-end demo with a seeded regression shows rollback within 10 minutes at 0.1% exposure.
notes: Align with ENG on offline replay harness for shadow scoring (ENG-4102).
Tie into Console rollout UI for manual overrides and audit (UX work in DES-412).
Consider privacy for mirrored requests — strip PII before shadowing where required.
